questions.q: Why do interface tables need periodic purging?
options: Because unmanaged accumulation of old rows can slow future imports and make it hard to tell which rows belong to which load
Because Oracle Fusion charges extra for unused rows
Because interface tables automatically delete themselves after one use
Purging is never actually necessary
questions.explain: Without deliberate cleanup, interface tables can grow with stale data from many past loads, creating confusion and potential performance issues.

questions.q: What does the 'purge only successfully processed records' option remove?
options: Every row in the interface table regardless of status
Nothing — this option does not exist
Only rows that were never attempted
Only rows that already became real application records, since there's no further reason to keep their staged copy
questions.explain: This narrower, lower-risk option clears rows that have already successfully become real records, since their staged copy no longer serves a purpose.

questions.q: What is the real risk described in this lesson around purging interface data?
options: Purging is too slow to be practical
Purging can accidentally create new supplier records
Purging rejected rows before reviewing and correcting them destroys the evidence needed to diagnose and fix the problem
Purging is always completely safe regardless of timing
questions.explain: The danger isn't technical complexity — it's purging too early, before the rejected row's data and error detail have been read and acted on.

questions.q: Why might the 'purge all matching records' option require scoping parameters like a source and group identifier?
options: Because Oracle requires a minimum of three parameters for every purge
To avoid accidentally sweeping up data from a different, unrelated load
Because this option purges the entire Oracle Fusion environment by default
Scoping parameters are never required for this option
questions.explain: Scoping parameters narrow a more aggressive purge to the specific batch intended, preventing it from clearing unrelated data by mistake.

questions.q: Where does purging fit in the overall FBDI workflow described in this lesson?
options: It should happen once a batch is fully resolved — after rejections are reviewed, corrected, resubmitted, and confirmed successful
It should be the very first step, before running any import
It should replace the need for reviewing the execution report entirely
It should never be performed under any circumstances
questions.explain: The safe sequence is: run the import, review results, correct and resubmit rejections, confirm success, and only then purge — not before issues are resolved.
